title: Power-quotient tensor coordinates and faithful flatness
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $d\geq1$ an integer, and $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in R$. Put $f=T^d+\sum_{i<d}a_iT^i\in R[T]$ and $B=R[T]/(f)$, with its canonical $R$-algebra structure and $t$ the class of $T$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The family $(t^i)_{0\leq i<d}$ is an $R$-basis of $B$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Write $c_i:B\to R$ for its unique coefficient maps, so $b=\sum_{i<d}c_i(b)t^i$. For every $R$-module $N$ there is an $R$-linear isomorphism
$$\Phi_N:B\otimes_RN\xrightarrow{\sim}N^d,\qquad b\otimes x\longmapsto(c_i(b)x)_{i<d},\qquad \Phi_N^{-1}((x_i)_{i<d})=\sum_{i<d}t^i\otimes x_i,$$
using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every $R$-linear $h:N\to N'$, one has $\Phi_{N'}(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes h)=h^d\Phi_N$, where $h^d$ applies $h$ in each coordinate. For every pair of $R$-linear maps $N_1\xrightarrow{h}N_2\xrightarrow{k}N_3$ with $kh=0$, the tensor sequence with $B$ is exact at $B\otimes_RN_2$ if and only if $\operatorname{im}h=\ker k$. Thus $R\to B$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. All assertions include the zero ring, with the specified index set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$ even there.

proof.text: If R is nontrivial, Polynomial.degree_sum_fin_lt shows the lower-degree sum has degree less than d. Thus f is monic of natural degree d. The basis of AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] has the specified powers as vectors. If R is subsingleton, so is its unital module B; use the linear equivalence between the singleton modules B and (Fin d → R), and Basis.ofEquivFun. Its basis vectors equal the specified powers by subsingleton elimination. The polynomial and quotient are those of [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and the basis uses [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

proof.text: Since d ≥ 1, Fin d is nonempty. Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat.finsupp makes (Fin d →₀ R) faithfully flat, including when R is zero. Transfer this along e.repr using Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_linearEquiv. Then Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_exact_iff_exact identifies tensor exactness with original exactness. LinearMap.exact_iff identifies the latter with ker k = range h; symmetry of equality yields the displayed range h = ker k. The supplied zero-composite assumption is unnecessary for this stronger Mathlib equivalence.

lean.statement: theorem exists_monicQuotient_faithful_tensor_coordinates (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (a : Fin d → R) (f : R[X]) (hf : f = X ^ d + ∑ i : Fin d, C (a i) * X ^ (i : ℕ)) : ∃ e : Module.Basis (Fin d) R (AdjoinRoot f), (∀ i : Fin d, e i = root f ^ (i : ℕ)) ∧ (∀ b : AdjoinRoot f, b = ∑ i : Fin d, e.coord i b • root f ^ (i : ℕ)) ∧ (∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N], (∀ (b : AdjoinRoot f) (x : N) (i : Fin d), ((TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft e).trans (Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite R N (Fin d))) (b ⊗ₜ[R] x) i = e.coord i b • x) ∧ (∀ x : Fin d → N, ((TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft e).trans (Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite R N (Fin d))).symm x = ∑ i : Fin d, (root f ^ (i : ℕ)) ⊗ₜ[R] x i)) ∧ (∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (N' : Type w) [AddCommGroup N'] [Module R N'] (h : N →ₗ[R] N') (q : AdjoinRoot f ⊗[R] N) (i : Fin d), ((TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft e).trans (Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite R N' (Fin d))) (h.lTensor (AdjoinRoot f) q) i = h (((TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft e).trans (Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite R N (Fin d))) q i)) ∧ (∀ (N₁ : Type v) [AddCommGroup N₁] [Module R N₁] (N₂ : Type w) [AddCommGroup N₂] [Module R N₂] (N₃ : Type z) [AddCommGroup N₃] [Module R N₃] (h : N₁ →ₗ[R] N₂) (k : N₂ →ₗ[R] N₃), k.comp h = 0 → (Function.Exact (h.lTensor (AdjoinRoot f)) (k.lTensor (AdjoinRoot f)) ↔ LinearMap.range h = LinearMap.ker k)) ∧ RingHom.FaithfullyFlat (algebraMap R (AdjoinRoot f))
